title: Microsoft Teams: decline an incoming mobile call with a message
summary: The briefing agrees with Microsoft's supplied notice and roadmap, including automatic availability and the expected rollout window. The calling-policy path and PowerShell command are documented, and targeted searches found no separate switch or licensing requirement for the new option.

claims.claim: Teams mobile users will be able to decline an incoming Teams call and send a message to the caller at the same time.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice describes a new communication method and asks organisations to review the change as appropriate.
claims.quote: This change provides a new way for users to communicate by allowing a user declining an eligible Teams call to send a predefined or custom message to the caller through Teams chat. Review this change as appropriate for your organization.

claims.claim: The response appears in Teams chat so users can continue the conversation.
claims.quote: The response will appear in Teams chat so users can continue the conversation after the call is declined.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The supplied notice does not describe whether compliance controls treat these responses differently from other chat messages.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams decline incoming call message mobile retention eDiscovery permission app version predefined responses customize. Read all of MC1540349, including its compliance section: it asks for review but gives no different retention, eDiscovery or communication-compliance treatment.

claims.claim: The supplied notice does not describe a new identity for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams decline incoming call message mobile retention eDiscovery permission app version predefined responses customize. Read the complete supplied MC1540349: it describes a user sending the response and names no new identity.

claims.claim: The supplied notice does not describe a new permission for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams decline incoming call message mobile retention eDiscovery permission app version predefined responses customize. Read the complete supplied MC1540349: no new permission is named.

claims.claim: The control is at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Edit > Make private calls.
claims.quote: select Voice > Calling policies. ... Select the policy or policies that you want to modify, and then select Edit. ... Make private calls - This setting controls all calling capabilities in Teams.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowPrivateCalling $false disables calling through a MicrosoftTeams calling policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy ... [-Identity] <string> ... [-AllowPrivateCalling <boolean>] ... Controls all calling capabilities in Teams. Turning this off will turn off all calling functionality in Teams.

claims.claim: Calling policies can be assigned to users, including directly or through groups.
claims.quote: You can assign a policy directly to users, either individually or at scale through a batch assignment (if supported for the policy type), or to a group that the users are members of (if supported for the policy type).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning off Make private calls prevents users with that policy from receiving incoming calls.
claims.quote: If the Make private calls setting is turned off in the calling policy, users with that policy can't see the Calls app in their Teams client, can't escalate Chat conversations to audio calls, and can't receive incoming calls.

claims.claim: Users with Make private calls turned off cannot see the Calls app.
claims.quote: If the Make private calls setting is turned off in the calling policy, users with that policy can't see the Calls app in their Teams client

claims.claim: Users with Make private calls turned off cannot escalate chat conversations to audio calls.
claims.quote: users with that policy can't see the Calls app in their Teams client, can't escalate Chat conversations to audio calls, and can't receive incoming calls.

claims.claim: Make private calls controls all Teams calling functionality, rather than only the new message option.
claims.quote: Make private calls - This setting controls all calling capabilities in Teams. Turn this setting off to turn off all calling functionality in Teams.

claims.claim: The notice does not say whether administrators can edit the predefined responses.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams decline incoming call message mobile retention eDiscovery permission app version predefined responses customize; "Teams" "decline" "message" "policy". Read MC1540349 and Teams calling policies; the notice lists examples without administrator editing instructions.

claims.claim: The notice does not say whether its three response examples form a complete or localised list.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams decline incoming call message mobile retention eDiscovery permission app version predefined responses customize. Read all of MC1540349: its list says 'such as' and does not address completeness or localisation.

claims.claim: Disabling incoming Teams calls through Make private calls also removes the incoming-call opportunity to use the message option.
claims.quote: If the Make private calls setting is turned off in the calling policy, users with that policy can't see the Calls app in their Teams client, can't escalate Chat conversations to audio calls, and can't receive incoming calls.
